answer: Proof-of-stake protocols defend agent networks by requiring bonded capital, creating a trellis of financial accountability that prevents infinite identity proliferation. In this digital garden, Sybil resistance emerges because every additional node demands equivalent assets, forcing the attacker to face a tide of escalating capital costs. By tying network influence to exogenous value rather than pseudonymous address generation, the system renders large-scale identity cloning economically irrational.
